title: Airport Pickup Without Mobile Data: Make a Backup Plan
description: Plan an airport pickup when roaming, mobile data or your phone may fail: save the instructions, agree a contact fallback and confirm where to wait.
cta: Make the connection before you make the journey.
image_alt: An unbranded charcoal suitcase with a pale travel folder beside airport seating and large sunlit terminal windows.
body:
Before flying, save your ride confirmation offline and agree with the transportation provider how you will connect if mobile data is unavailable. Include the exact pickup instructions, a contact method you can actually use and an agreed place to wait if contact fails. Airport Wi-Fi can help, but it should not be the only way to find your ride.

This is especially useful when arriving from overseas, changing SIMs or traveling with a phone that may run out of power. A flight number tells the provider which arrival you mean; it does not tell them that you have collected your bags or reached the agreed pickup point.

Save a small offline pickup pack

Download or screenshot the details while you still have a reliable connection. Open the saved copy before departure to check that it works without loading a website. If your phone may be unusable, keep the essential information on paper as well.

  • Reservation: provider name, confirmation reference and the full local pickup date.
  • Arrival: airport and final inbound flight, including the operating airline if your ticket uses a codeshare number.
  • Instructions: terminal, level and exact approved meeting or vehicle pickup point supplied for your reservation.
  • Contacts: the provider's reservation/day-of-trip number, with country code, and the communication channel you agreed to use.
  • Destination: complete address and any hotel or venue entrance details.
  • Fallback: where to wait and how to ask for updated instructions if you cannot make contact.

Keep the confirmation private. Avoid posting a booking reference, travel document or personal contact information in a public group to ask for help.

Separate mobile data from calls and messages

A phone can have working Wi-Fi while its normal number cannot receive a call or text. It can also make ordinary calls while mobile data is disabled. Check the arrangements for your own handset and mobile plan before travel; do not assume that installing a messaging app makes you reachable.

Tell the provider which number will work after landing and whether you expect to use ordinary calls, SMS or an agreed internet messaging channel. Ask whether that channel is supported. If a companion will be the reachable contact, get their agreement and have the provider confirm the arrangement before the trip.

A useful preflight question: “My phone may have Wi-Fi only after landing. Which contact method should I use, and what should I do if I cannot connect?” A sent message is not confirmation that someone has read or accepted the plan.

Use airport Wi-Fi as a connection opportunity

SFO's official Wi-Fi page lists free service in all terminals and explains how to connect. Follow the airport's current instructions and verify the network against its published information or airport signage. Other airports have their own arrangements; check the airport you will actually use.

While connected inside the terminal, send a short status update and obtain the pickup instructions before walking outside. Wi-Fi coverage or your connection may change as you move. Do not assume an airport connection continues at the curb or inside the vehicle.

If you cannot connect, ask airport information staff where you can get communications assistance. They may be able to point you to an appropriate resource; they do not replace your transportation provider or confirm a private reservation.

Agree the waiting point before you need it

Ask the provider to distinguish a place where you can wait from the location where a vehicle can collect you. Do not choose an arbitrary door or walk between terminals looking for a car. Use the instructions for the airport, service and reservation you have booked.

At SFO, the airport says terminal curbs are for active pickup and drop-off, and vehicles cannot wait there. Its current travel alerts direct waiting drivers to the cell phone waiting lot. That is not a passenger meeting point or permission to walk to it. Confirm the actual connection with your provider.

Illustrative example: your saved plan identifies an indoor waiting location and a provider contact method. After collecting your bags, you connect to terminal Wi-Fi and send your terminal, baggage status and exact location. Follow the acknowledged pickup instructions. If the message does not go through, use the fallback you agreed rather than silently moving to another door.

If the flight or contact plan changes

Send the final inbound flight, airport and full local arrival date as soon as you can. Our flight-change guide explains how to resolve the existing ride's status; the overnight pickup-date checklist helps with midnight arrivals.

If you need alternative transportation, try to establish what happens to the original reservation and its applicable terms first. Do not assume silence cancels a ride, that a second request replaces it or that a provider can wait indefinitely. For a traveler booked by someone else, share the offline plan directly with the passenger using our passenger handoff checklist.

For a new journey, explore Koast airport transfers and request a quote that includes your arrival and communication needs. For an existing Koast ride, use the contact on your reservation confirmation or the agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment of changes. A new quote does not amend the original booking.
